findings.required: Use production RESPONSE_BYTES=40 and the exact unsafe ResponseMemory signatures physical(&self)->u64, address(&mut self)->*mut u8, unsafe release(self), and verification_owner()->Option<Claim>. Bind an eight-byte-aligned guarded owned backing, exclusive complete Claim identity and external quarantine ownership through unfinished Drop; consuming release removes bookkeeping once without reading response bytes.

Invent no constructor or insertion API. Exercise Mailbox::new, open_worker(tid), admit(request, claim), reserve(handle), copied(handle, serial, true), verification_read16, observer select and return_value. Worker is nongeneric; private assertions and real cancel_pending belong in a module-local cfg(test) module in generated smp_application_syscall.rs.

In generated application_syscall.rs place one test helper immediately before the second compare_exchange(2,1,...) in verification_prepare_retained, and record a status event immediately after Completion::publish's final status store without dereferencing released memory. Second-CAS failure returns -71 and may preserve prefix writes.

Generated stability_phase.rs may expose only a module-local cfg(test) setter taking (stage:u64, commits:u64, invalid:i32). Run every row in a fresh process because observer and fault statics are one-shot; baseline address/drop/claim counters after preparation.

A runner-owned atomic clock backs kernel::bindings::ktime_get()->i64. At t selected wake publication returns -11 with one fault attempt and zero real send callbacks; retain through t+1,999,999,999 and publish/release once at t+2,000,000,000. Precommit cancellation returns -71, latches first invalid -125 and retains/quarantines; committed cancellation preserves the completion for recovery. Mode 2 publishes then its matching notification fails once with -5; cover wake None separately.

Enumerate only the three generated candidate files per mode plus explicitly named fresh runner, allocator/clock shim, owned-memory ledger, parser and manifest files. Bind exact paths, hook signatures, row IDs and expected event sequences. std allocation stays in the host runner and hooks disappear under cfg(not(test)).
